name: babok
summary: For business analysts (IIBA BABOK v3 vocabulary): elicit, analyse, specify, verify, validate, approve. Docodego's 01-document is the BABOK's working vocabulary already — this pack says so in the record's own voice, and names the sponsor where the sign happens.
law: Words change. The contract does not: paths, file names, statuses, command names, exit codes, and diagnostic codes are identical in every pack. The sixteen statutes are recorded verbatim and are never re-voiced.

01-document.gloss: business needs elicited, analysed, and specified

02-compose.gloss: the solution increment, built and kept shippable

04-govern.gloss: the value loop closed: monitor, measure, improve

streams.01-document/01-discover: [Finding] business needs elicited from stakeholders, before any register exists · producer: anyone with a need → consumer: 02-refine
streams.01-document/02-refine: [Finding] requirements analysis — elicit, analyse, specify, prioritise · producer: the analyst with stakeholders → consumer: 04-plan
streams.01-document/03-validate: [Grounding] assumptions tested before commitment — validate cheap, before solution design · producer: analysis work → consumer: a specified, prioritised requirement
streams.01-document/04-plan: [Grounding] solution planning — what enters this delivery cycle · producer: the analyst + sponsor → consumer: 02-compose/01-build
streams.02-compose/01-build: [Rising] the solution increment, built tests-first · producer: specified requirements + compose → consumer: 02-integrate
streams.02-compose/02-integrate: [Rising] keep it shippable — merged, green, reviewed · producer: 01-build → consumer: 01-demo
streams.02-compose/03-enhance: [Nurturing] improvements from stakeholder feedback into the cycle · producer: demo feedback → consumer: 01-build
streams.02-compose/04-maintain: [Nurturing] defect fixes and technical debt, never starved · producer: incidents, retro actions → consumer: 01-build
streams.03-demonstrate/01-demo: [Nurturing] the solution demonstrated — working software, to stakeholders · producer: 02-integrate → consumer: 02-accept
streams.03-demonstrate/02-accept: [Nurturing] acceptance criteria verified, the sponsor approves · producer: 01-demo → consumer: 03-release
streams.04-govern/01-monitor: [Nurturing] production tells the truth · producer: 04-deploy → consumer: 02-measure
streams.04-govern/02-measure: [Leaving] outcomes against the business need — outcomes only, never person-scores · producer: 01-monitor → consumer: 03-retrospect
streams.04-govern/03-retrospect: [Leaving] the lessons-learned round · producer: the whole team → consumer: 04-improve
streams.04-govern/04-improve: [Leaving] improvement actions land here, each with an owner · producer: 03-retrospect → consumer: the next analysis cycle — the loop closes

gateQuestions.GQ-1: What business need does this requirement serve, in one sentence a stakeholder can verify?
gateQuestions.GQ-2: What evidence proves each acceptance criterion actually ran — verified in the build, validated with stakeholders?
gateQuestions.GQ-3: What is the biggest risk to this requirement delivering value — and its mitigation?
gateQuestions.GQ-4: What did you explicitly exclude from solution scope?

glossary.business need: a unit's intent — the `## intent` section of spec.md
glossary.requirement: a unit — the folder whose spec.md carries the need, scope, acceptance, and risks
glossary.elicitation: 01-document/01-discover — needs gathered before any register exists
glossary.solution scope: a spec's `## scope` section — in and out, explicitly
glossary.risk: a spec's `## threats` section — each risk with its mitigation
glossary.specify: authoring spec.md — the requirement specification, scored by `docodego score`
glossary.verification: did we build it right — the check and lint passes, the proofs on disk
glossary.validation: did we build the right thing — 03-demonstrate/02-accept, criteria met against stakeholders
glossary.approval: 03-demonstrate/02-accept — the sponsor signs; `docodego deliver` records it
glossary.traceability: `docodego trace <unit>` — one requirement's whole arc on one timeline
glossary.stakeholder: anyone with a need — the producer of 01-discover and the audience of 01-demo
glossary.recommended actions: 04-govern/04-improve — improvement actions, each with an owner
glossary.BABOK v3: IIBA, A Guide to the Business Analysis Body of Knowledge — this pack's dialect source; docodego is not affiliated with or endorsed by the IIBA
